The write-ahead log, or WAL, in a databaseâs storage system is a list of all the changes in the database, or records that are about to be written to disk. The WAL helps a database recover after a crash by reducing the amount of work to be done after the database is restored to a consistent state. If the database crashes, the WAL is used to apply the transactions in the order they were written, ensuring that the database is restored to a consistent state. This approach minimizes the amount of data to be recovered and reduces the time to recover the database.
The WAL also prevents a situation known as a âdirty readâ in which a database recovery process reads half-written data that was not yet flushed to disk before the crash occurred. Instead, the WAL approach ensures that a transaction is completely written to disk before it is considered committed, preventing any intermediate states. This ensures that the database recovery process can always apply a transaction in its entirety, as intended, which helps maintain the consistency of the database.
